purpose: How unusual are this many positive paired changes under a fair-sign model?
meaning: Compute each shifted after-reading minus its paired before-reading. Omit exact zeros, count k positives among n nonzero pairs, and sum the fair binomial masses from k through n for the predeclared positive-direction alternative.

definition.setting: A workshop measures six pieces before and after adjusting a gauge. The same pieces stay paired. Choose either different original changes or originally matching readings; add a common after-reading shift h. Follow each pair into a positive, negative or zero difference, then count the null sign patterns with at least as many positives.

signature.h: Common added after-reading shift in mm
signature.a_i: Unshifted after-reading for pair i in mm
signature.b_i: Before-reading for the same pair in mm
signature.d_i: Shifted after minus before for one pair in mm
signature.n: Number of nonzero differences after exact ties are omitted
signature.K: Positive-sign count under the conditional fair-sign null
signature.j: Bound summation index over possible positive-sign counts
signature.p_+: One-sided null tail probability for at least k positive signs

conditions: Six constructed pairs use independent-pair and conditional fair-sign assumptions: under the null each nonzero difference has probability 1/2 of either sign. A continuous difference distribution with median zero supplies the usual median interpretation. This does not assert equality of the raw before/after medians. A nonzero difference lost in a represented after-reading is a precision failure. Exact zeros are omitted; with substantial ties the conditional fair-sign model needs separate justification. All ties provide no sign evidence. The alternative, positive differences, is one-sided and predeclared; interactive exploration is not an inferential study.
